shortDescription: FuelCell Energy NASDAQ:FCEL was reinstated Wednesday with a Buy rating at Craig-Hallum, which set a $22 price target, after the firm had dropped coverage of the fuel cell manufacturer in early 2024 because of "a disorganized product focus and bleak product revenue outlook given very minimal/no prod…

children: was reinstated Wednesday with a Buy rating at Craig-Hallum, which set a $22 price target, after the firm had dropped coverage of the fuel cell manufacturer in early 2024 because of "a disorganized product focus and bleak product revenue outlook given very minimal/no product backlog" and a fuel cell offering that was "ill-matched to its target commercial and industrial end markets."

The company was aggressively focused on building out its Generation Portfolio, largely because it was mostly unable to sell its fuel cell systems outright unless in heavily subsidized markets, Craig-Hallum analyst Eric Stine said, adding the buildout was time-consuming and capital-intensive, and profitability appeared unattainable without product-driven revenue growth and margin improvement.

"So why reinstate now? Simply put, it is the emerging data center opportunity, for which we think FCEL's carbonate fuel cell platform is well-suited, which brings a clear path to potentially significant product revenue and (eventual) profitability," Stine wrote.
"With investor interest in behind-the-meter solutions for AI/data center applications growing by the day," FuelCell Energy

"deserves a seat at the table," the analyst said, as its product offering is "now a strong fit as a data center power solution for continuous/baseload power generation, given it is a DC-native power source with high energy density, high efficiency, inherent redundancy, and quiet operations."

title: FuelCell Energy reinstated with Buy rating at Craig-Hallum on emerging data center opportunity
